thread:
Sam: Heads-up — OptimaApp reported a spike of 401s this morning after they upgraded to our new mobile SDK. They say the SDK started sending an X-Api-Fingerprint header and our gateway is returning `invalid_api_key`. Repro and headers below.

Sam: curl they ran:
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz123456" \
  -H "X-Api-Fingerprint: sha256:2a7f3b...c9d" \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions
```

Sam: Response body:
```json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not recognized"}
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

Jordan: Thanks — can you paste the gateway request-id or proxy logs if available? Curious whether auth rejected because key not found or because fingerprint check failed. Also which SDK version they upgraded to?

Sam: Got a small log from their customer: `req_id=01GZ2X... auth=reject reason=FP_MISMATCH key_id=sk_live_AbCd...` — looks like fingerprint mismatch rather than key missing. SDK version is `redwood-mobile@2.1.0` (they rolled yesterday).

Ravi: @Sam thanks. We started a canary of auth-proxy v2 yesterday which added optional fingerprint enforcement. Looks like one of the canary hosts accidentally had enforcement set to `enforce` (should have been `warn`). That would convert a missing/incorrect fingerprint into a hard reject -> 401 `invalid_api_key`. I'll check rollout and rollback.

Jordan: In the meantime we should either tell the customer how to compute the fingerprint the proxy expects or advise them to stop sending the header. To compute (hex sha256 prefix):
```bash
# compute expected fingerprint for a key value
echo -n "sk_live_AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz123456" | sha256sum | awk '{print "sha256:"substr($1,1,64)}'
```
Share that with them — if their header doesn't match exactly (case sensitive, no extra whitespace) it'll fail.

Sam: Copying that to OptimaApp now. They say the SDK computes the fingerprint using base64(sha256) not hex, and also appends a `=` padding char. So two possible mismatches: encoding (hex vs base64) and trailing padding.

Ravi: Yep, that explains it — our current DB stores the fingerprint as `sha256:<hex-hex>`; the canary enforcement expects hex. Two options: 1) rollback the canary enforcement to `warn` ASAP (short-term), 2) make the validation accept both hex and base64 variants (longer-term) or normalize on ingestion. I'll start rollback now.

AuthBot: Incident INC-2026-1234 created: "Auth-proxy canary enforcing fingerprint -> customer 401s". Assigned to Ravi.

Ravi: Rolling back the canary host with env var `FINGERPRINT_ENFORCEMENT=warn` on host `auth-proxy-canary-3`. ETA ~8m. I'll post when done.

Sam: Noted — told OptimaApp to temporarily disable the header or downgrade the SDK to 2.0.x. They're OK with that for now.

Jordan: Follow-up: after rollback we should add a unit test to the validation that accepts both `sha256:<hex>` and `sha256:<base64>` with/without padding and trim whitespace. Also add a metric to track FP_MISMATCH rejections so we catch this earlier.

Ravi: Agreed. Rolling back now, will open a PR to normalize on hex + add compatibility layer.

Sam: Thanks team :pray: will close the customer loop once rollback is confirmed.
